leads.summary: The tunnel fallback ignores wired transport and chooses any associated Wi-Fi, not the underlying uplink
leads.consequence: When `ip route get 1.1.1.1` returns a TUN/PPP and the actual main-route transport is Ethernet, the new helper returns the tunnel (displayed as `ethernet Meta`) if there is no connected Wi-Fi; if a Wi-Fi NIC happens to be associated alongside Ethernet, it instead selects that Wi-Fi although traffic travels over wired Ethernet. Bar label, Wi-Fi QR menu guard, speed-test label and network details describe the wrong connection. Choose the physical device from the routing table/underlying route (or expose ambiguous uplinks) rather than arbitrarily preferring Wi-Fi.

leads.summary: After replacing `iface` with Wi-Fi, verbose status still publishes the tunnel's IP address and gateway
leads.consequence: With a TUN route and connected Wi-Fi, `iface`, prefix, bytes, and type describe the Wi-Fi NIC while `ip` and `gateway` are taken from the original TUN route. A panel user sees and can copy a VPN-private IP/gateway under the Wi-Fi header; router latency probes target that virtual gateway. The verified synthetic case reports `iface wlp3s0`, `ip 10.10.10.5`, `gateway 10.10.10.1` even though the Wi-Fi interface has `192.0.2.5/24`. Re-derive IP, gateway and gateway ping for the chosen physical interface, or present route and physical-interface fields separately.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; one sentence in N1 Impact

leads.summary: NetworkManager's `connected (externally)` Wi-Fi state is discarded by the new selector
leads.consequence: NetworkManager emits `connected (externally)` for an activated externally configured connection. The new equality `$3 == "connected"` returns no Wi-Fi for this real state. Behind a tunnel the bar falls through to `ethernet <TUN>` and verbose reports the tunnel, even with an associated Wi-Fi interface. Unlike bin/omarchy-network-band's `nm_get`, this new call also lacks `LC_ALL=C`, so translated STATE values will not match under a localized session. Normalize locale and accept the activated external state, preferably query numeric connection state or match its documented variants.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_partly; connected (externally) edge not published (minor); LC_ALL claim contradicted by Opus (terse nmcli not translated, nmcli utils.h:289-299)

leads.summary: A legal UUID- or address-shaped Bluetooth alias hides a human-named device
leads.consequence: BlueZ accepts arbitrary nonempty Alias strings and the patch prioritizes the alias as `deviceLabel`. `hasHumanName` filters based solely on that label, so an address- or UUID-shaped alias of a device whose advertised `deviceName` is `MX Master 3S` now causes `deviceLists` to drop even a connected or paired device. Its row vanishes, and if it is the only connected device the panel's connected-state icon also vanishes; the panel cannot connect, disconnect or forget it until the alias is reset with another tool. Before the change the advertised human name won; #7837 independently proposes testing both names. Keep the alias for display, but consider both names when deciding whether the device is human-named.
leads.triage: behavioural_followup_confirmed; Optional note; low likelihood per Opus (BlueZ never stores such alias itself)

leads.summary: A nonzero BlueZ PairableTimeout expires while the panel is still open
leads.consequence: PairableTimeout defaults to zero but is a configurable per-adapter value. When it is nonzero, BlueZ turns Pairable off after that many seconds; this panel only writes Pairable on open, adapter/bar/power change, or when discovery retry fires. If discovery stays active, no retry fires, and no onPairableChanged handler reasserts it. The user can leave the panel visibly open and scanning yet incoming pairing stops working until they close/reopen it. Decide whether to set/restore the timeout, reassert on expiry, or explicitly document the timeout constraint; avoid an unbounded reactive write loop.
leads.triage: behavioural_followup_confirmed; folded into B2 hypothesis section; non-default config

leads.summary: Open Steam PR #11981 conflicts with this rule and makes this PR's Steam test false after integration
leads.consequence: #11981 (currently open and separately mergeable into quattro, heads diverged) removes the unqualified `o.window("steam", { float = true, idle_inhibit = "fullscreen" })` in favour of title-scoped floating, applies idle inhibition to `steam.*` and `gamescope`, and intentionally avoids floating games whose class is `steam`. A three-way merge using the real common file yields conflict markers on the whole steam.lua file. Simply taking its rule to resolve this conflicts with this PR's test at line 16, while preserving this PR's unqualified floating rule defeats #11981's fix. Coordinate the rule and adapt assertions if either merges first.

leads.summary: Open network PRs require integrating competing interface selectors and test expectations
leads.consequence: #12071 and #8866 already propose physical interface selection for TUN/policy routes, including Ethernet, instead of this PR's Wi-Fi-only replacement. #8476 adds an explicit --iface Wi-Fi selector that must not be overwritten by automatic tunnel selection, and #9809 modifies frequency parsing alongside the changed status script. The PRs are diverged, each is MERGEABLE against quattro, yet three-way merging each against this pinned head leaves unresolved conflicts (2, 2, 2, 1 hunks respectively); simply resolving by keeping one selector drops another feature or its test. Pick one physical-route policy and preserve explicit interface selection and MLO parsing when integrating. This is an integration warning, not a claim that an automatic GitHub merge has already happened.
leads.triage: factual_verified_partly; #12071 and #8866 published in N1 suggestion; #8476/#9809 overlap (network-band-test.sh add/add, status script) not published as low value

leads.summary: Open Bluetooth agent PR #12897 reintroduces a pre-bar Pairable=false write during panel construction
leads.consequence: The open, diverged #12897 registers a new Just Works agent whose consent gate is Pairable, and adds `Component.onCompleted: syncPairable()`. `syncPairable` computes `opened || openSibling() !== null`, but an unopened widget's `bar` has not been injected yet, so `openSibling()` returns null and it writes Pairable=false even when a sibling monitor's panel is open. This PR explicitly guards against that pre-bar write and reasserts after injection. The Panel.qml three-way merge has two conflict hunks. If both changes land, preserve the early guard and sibling reassertion, plus the agent's new behavior; do not resolve the conflict by simply taking #12897's construction-time write.
leads.triage: factual_verified; published as overlap; #12897 same author also marked Fixes #7889

leads.summary: New tunnel test passes when neither production status path ever substitutes Wi-Fi
leads.consequence: The test copies `is_tunnel_iface` into a local shell function instead of executing the status command. The remaining checks only grep for identifiers/calls. In a disposable production script where the `prefer_wifi_over_tunnel` branch is guarded by `if false && is_tunnel_iface`, every assertion still passes even though both bar and verbose always show the tunnel. Add stubbed `ip`, `nmcli`, `iw` and synthetic sysfs and assert the actual command's normal/verbose outputs for TUN+Wi-Fi, TUN+Ethernet and a non-tunnel route.

leads.summary: Steam source-text assertion passes with the new rule commented out
leads.consequence: The test searches for a line beginning `o.window` without stripping Lua block comments or loading the Lua rule. Wrapping exactly the new `o.window("steam_app_.*", ...)` line in `--[[ ... ]]` leaves all four assertions green while Hyprland never receives an idle-inhibit rule for games. Load steam.lua with an `hl.window_rule` collector, or strip Lua comments and test the actual registered rule. The related #9667 test already strips line/block comments.
leads.triage: dropped; test passes with rule inside Lua block comment; contrived mutation, low value

# RETRO: PR #12114

## What worked
- Running the Sol hunt in parallel added value in two ways:
  - It found the related open PRs (#12071, #8866, #11981, #12897, #7837). One of them (#12071) already implements the fix that Opus suggested for N1.
  - It found two behavioural leads (the alias-shaped label and a nonzero PairableTimeout). Opus confirmed both at source level in one neutral follow-up.
- The Opus self-check caught one wrong claim, which came from the coordinator's paraphrase of final.md B2 ("registered or removed"). It also caught several lost qualifiers (the BR/EDR key-persistence exceptions, LE versus Classic, the write-loop bound). All were fixed before the editorial check.

## Avoidable friction
- At bootstrap, the coordinator's first command listed the assignment and printed the full `team-1.json` (138 KB, mostly history) in one call. Claude Code persisted the output to its native tool-results store; the content is the team registry. This is a recorded storage deviation. Fix: read the registry with `jq` projections of the needed fields only.
- The first editorial check returned revise because the tunnel-detection finding had no **Impact** paragraph. Drafting check: every `###` finding needs an explicit Impact line, even when the bullets already imply it.
- No Markdown renderer is installed (neither python-markdown nor pandoc), so a small assignment-local `render_reader.py` builds `reader.html`. A shared renderer in review-team would avoid rewriting one each round.

## Process deviations
- Coordinator: the oversized output described above.
- Opus reviewer: it ran `bash -n` once on the host against its own fixture script (no PR code). This is disclosed in final.md, has no evidence impact, and no run depends on it.

## Carry forward
- When summarising a reviewer's mechanism claim ("sets X when Y"), keep both directions. The self-check caught "registered or removed" here.
comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** four of the five changes do what they claim. The tunnel handling in `omarchy-network-status` fixes the Wi-Fi-under-VPN case, but it also changes the reported network in a common docked-laptop setup where the base reported Ethernet. The pairable lifecycle has one side effect outside the panel plus an unconfirmed gap, and several new tests stay green when the behaviour they describe is removed.

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `steam_app_.*` idle-inhibit rule | **Verified** from source: Hyprland 0.56.2 matches classes with `RE2::FullMatch`, so `"steam"` never matched games, and Proton's X11 driver sets the class `steam_app_<id>`. Native Linux games and Proton's Wayland driver use other class names. |
| `omarchy-network-band` SSID decode | **Verified** in a stubbed run: `printf %b` exactly inverts iw's `print_ssid_escaped`. Head lists `2.4 5` for accented, CJK, emoji, backslash, `\x41`-lookalike, edge-space and tab SSIDs, where the base lists only `5`. Non-UTF-8 SSIDs still fail to match, which is pre-existing. |
| Bluetooth alias-first label | **Verified** from source: Quickshell maps `name` to BlueZ `Alias` and `deviceName` to `Name`, so a user rename is now shown. |
| Pairable open/close lifecycle | **Verified** from source for open, close, popout handoff between monitors, adapter power changes and destruction. `Bar.requestPopout` closes the old panel only after the new one is open, so the closing instance sees an open sibling and leaves Pairable on. |

### VPN over Ethernet with Wi-Fi still associated is now reported as Wi-Fi

`prefer_wifi_over_tunnel` swaps a tunnel route device for any connected Wi-Fi, without checking which link carries the tunnel. NetworkManager can keep Wi-Fi connected alongside Ethernet (default metrics: Ethernet 100, Wi-Fi 600), so a docked laptop running a full-tunnel VPN hits this case.

Stubbed `ip`/`nmcli`/`iw` and a synthetic sysfs tree (fixture names):

| Scenario | base | head |
|---|---|---|
| WireGuard over Wi-Fi | `ethernet wg0` | `wifi HomeNet …` (the intended fix) |
| Ethernet, Wi-Fi associated, no tunnel | `ethernet eth0` | `ethernet eth0` |
| WireGuard over Ethernet, no Wi-Fi | `ethernet wg0` | `ethernet wg0` |
| **WireGuard over Ethernet, Wi-Fi associated** | `ethernet wg0` | **`wifi HomeNet …`**; `--verbose`: `iface wlan0` with the idle Wi-Fi byte counters |

**Impact:** in that last case the network panel is titled with the SSID and computes Receiving/Sending from the idle Wi-Fi counters, so it shows near-zero throughput while traffic flows over Ethernet. The speed test is also titled with the SSID. In `--verbose` after any substitution, `ip` and `gateway` still come from the tunnel route while `iface`, `prefix` and the counters are Wi-Fi's. The bar's own network pill is NetworkManager-driven and does not read this script, so the visible changes are in the panel, the speed test and the menu's Wi-Fi QR entry rather than the bar.

**Suggested change:** when the route device is a tunnel, use the device of the lowest-metric non-tunnel default route in the main table (`ip -j route show table main default`), or at least prefer a connected wired device before Wi-Fi. That matches the panel's own "wired is preferred when both are up" rule. Open PR #12071 ("Show physical network behind TUN routes") already takes the main-table approach for both `print_status` and `print_verbose`, and #8866 also changes tunnel handling in this script, so the two approaches probably need reconciling.

### Tunnel detection misses TAP and catches modems

- `is_tunnel_iface` checks `<dev>/tun`, which the tun driver does not create. The tun driver registers an unnamed sysfs attribute group, so a TUN/TAP device has `tun_flags`, `owner` and `group` directly in its directory (`drivers/net/tun.c`).
- TAP devices are `ARPHRD_ETHER` (type 1), not 65534 as the comment says. In the stubbed run, a TAP VPN over Wi-Fi with the real sysfs layout (type 1 plus `tun_flags`) prints `ethernet tap0`.
- Type 65534 also covers raw-IP QMI modems (`qmi_wwan`), and 512 covers PPP/PPPoE. With Wi-Fi associated, a `wwan0` or `ppp0` default route is replaced by Wi-Fi. Replacing PPP is deliberate in the commit, but its message implies WWAN keeps its route device.

**Impact:** a TAP VPN over Wi-Fi is still reported as `ethernet tap0`, so the fix does not reach it. With Wi-Fi associated, a raw-IP WWAN or PPPoE default route is reported as Wi-Fi. NetworkManager prefers Wi-Fi over modems anyway, so the modem case is rare, but PPPoE (metric 460) beats Wi-Fi.

**Suggested change:** test `[[ -e $net_sysfs/$device/tun_flags ]]`, and fix the TUN/TAP comment. If modems and PPPoE should keep their route device, the route-based selection above also solves that, provided the tunnel test no longer treats `ppp0` or a raw-IP `wwan0` as a tunnel (for example by using NetworkManager's device type, as #12071 does).

### Pairable off also makes pairings started from this machine non-bonding

BlueZ documents Pairable as affecting only incoming pairing, but the kernel also applies it to pairings this machine starts (Linux v7.2, source-verified, no hardware run):

```text
Pairable=false  ->  HCI_BONDABLE cleared
  BR/EDR: IO-capability reply forced to no-bonding (hci_event.c)
          -> link key flushed at disconnect (unless the remote asks for
             dedicated bonding, or it is a legacy PIN pairing)
  LE:     SMP_AUTH_BONDING dropped from the pairing request (smp.c)
          -> keys not persistent
```

BlueZ's `Device.Pair` path does not raise Pairable.

**Impact:** pairing from the panel is fine while the panel is open. Pairing started with `omarchy bluetooth device pair <addr>`, `bluetoothctl pair` or another tool while the panel is closed now produces a pairing that is not kept: a Classic (BR/EDR) device loses it at disconnect, an LE device at the latest when bluetoothd restarts. So does a slow panel pairing that only begins after the panel is closed. Before this PR, Pairable stayed on while bt-agent was registered.

**Suggested change:** have `omarchy-bluetooth-device pair` turn Pairable on for the duration and restore it afterwards, or document that new devices should be paired from the panel.

### Hypothesis: BlueZ can turn Pairable back on while the panel is closed

With the stock `AlwaysPairable=false`, BlueZ 5.87 sets the adapter bondable whenever an agent becomes the default, and clears it when the last agent goes away (`src/agent.c`, `src/adapter.c`). So when `bt-agent` starts after the shell's first `false` write, or restarts on failure, Pairable is turned back on. The panel has no `onPairableChanged` handler, so Pairable would then stay on with the panel closed until the next open/close. A related case: with a non-default nonzero `PairableTimeout`, BlueZ turns Pairable off while the panel is still open and scanning, and nothing reasserts it.

**To settle:** after login, without opening the panel, run `bluetoothctl show | grep Pairable`; then restart `bt-agent` and check again.

**Suggested change (if confirmed):** in the existing `Connections { target: root.adapter }`, handle `onPairableChanged` by restarting a 1-second single-shot timer that calls `root.applyPairable()` whether the panel is open or closed. Equal-value writes are already skipped by `setPairable` and by Quickshell, so the panel cannot loop on its own; the timer limits any tug-of-war with another tool that forces the opposite value to about one write per second.

### Overlapping open PRs

- **#12897** (same author, also fixes #7889) implements pairable differently (`syncPairable`, plus `Component.onCompleted: syncPairable()` without this PR's `bar === null` guard) and edits the same `Panel.qml` region. Only one of the two approaches can land as-is.
- **#11981** moves `idle_inhibit = "fullscreen"` onto the `steam.*` rule (which already covers `steam_app_*`) and removes the unqualified `o.window("steam", …)` rule that `steam-idle-inhibit-test.sh` asserts.
- **#7837** also changes `deviceLabel` to prefer the alias, and additionally makes `hasHumanName` consider both names.

**Optional:** with the alias-first label, a device whose alias is MAC-, UUID- or whitespace-shaped while its `Name` is human-readable is now hidden from every panel section, including when connected (the base showed it under its `Name`). BlueZ never stores such an alias by itself, so this needs a client that saved one. Using the alias only when it passes the human-name check, otherwise `Name`, covers both directions. #7837 has the same goal but keeps the alias as the label and lets `hasHumanName` pass if either name is human.

**Optional test improvement:** these diagnostic mutants of head leave the tests green:
- `network-status-tun-test.sh` tests a copy of `is_tunnel_iface` and greps for function names. It never runs `omarchy-network-status` or uses the new `OMARCHY_NET_SYSFS` hook. It still passes with 65534 changed to 65535, with Wi-Fi never matched, and with the substitution moved after the wireless check. A stubbed run like `network-band-test.sh`, covering the four scenarios above, would pin the behaviour.
- The pairable regexes in `bluetooth-test.sh` still pass with the close-path `applyPairable()`, the open-path `applyPairable()`, `onEnabledChanged` or `onAdapterChanged` removed. The "open path" regex matches any later `applyPairable()` in the file. The `wantedPairable` truth table is behavioural and covers every branch.

`network-band-test.sh` and the label test fail on the base and on the matching mutants, as intended.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `33c7120c` against merge-base `2fbac0c8`, with upstream Hyprland 0.56.2, Linux v7.2, BlueZ 5.87, Quickshell 0.3.1, NetworkManager 1.58.1, iw and Proton source. The PR's tests, base overlays, diagnostic mutants and network-status/band scenarios ran in a sandbox with stubbed `ip`, `nmcli`, `iw` and a synthetic sysfs tree. There was no live Hyprland, Quickshell, BlueZ adapter, NetworkManager or radio: the Steam, label and Bluetooth findings are source-based, and the pairable hypothesis is untested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
